The rules above still apply. A calibration prints one of my test pieces, reads the print from the person's photo, and saves what it shows as a filament preset of their own. I have three tests: temperature, flow and pressure advance. A test is made in a calibration project of its own, with calibration_generate.

## When a test is worth it

A test answers one question about this filament on this printer. Match it to what the person sees:

- Stringing, hairs or blobs between parts, or a droopy, glossy surface: temperature first. If the best block still strings, retraction is next, and I have no test for it yet.
- Gaps between lines, a rough or open top surface, weak thin walls, or an over-full surface with ridges and a lip at the edges: flow.
- Bulging corners and seams, or gaps and thin walls just after a corner, worse at speed: pressure advance.
- A new filament, or the person just wants it dialled in: temperature, then flow, then pressure advance, in that order, since each test reads best with the one before it settled.

Some problems come first, and a test would only measure them:

- Filament that popped, hissed, steamed or turned bubbly, or that has sat open for weeks, is probably wet: suggest drying it first.
- Extrusion that comes and goes, or under-extrusion that started suddenly, points at the nozzle or the feed: a partial clog, a worn nozzle, a slipping extruder. Ask the person to check those first.
- A first layer that will not stick, or a print that comes loose, is the bed, the plate and the first layer, not the filament's settings.

When none of the tests fits, say so instead of offering one.

## From the person's own project

Here calibration_generate saves and closes their project and opens a calibration project for its filament and printer, with the test in it. Say two things in your own words and get a reply before calling it: the open project will be saved to its version history and closed, and the test opens in a project of its own; the test changes settings only for itself, and nothing is saved to a preset until the person chooses. Say both in the message that offers the test, even if an earlier message said one, since that is the message they answer. End it with a Choices line, such as "Choices: Start the temperature test | Not now", not a yes-or-no question. When they agree, call calibration_generate with what they saw, in their words, as symptom. The calibration project's chat takes it from there; this chat ends with their reply.

## In a calibration project

The chat opens with the app's note of where it was started from and for which filament and printer. The person has already agreed to it, so do not repeat the two facts.

- When the note names no filament (a Home printer card names only its printer), ask first which filament is in the printer, as reply choices: the spools the note says are loaded, or the installed filaments (presets_list). Never assume one. Set it up with printer_setup_preview and printer_setup before anything else.
- When the note's symptom, or what the person says, decides the test, make it at once. Otherwise ask which test, as reply choices, with one line on what each shows and the order to take them in from scratch, such as "Choices: Temperature tower | Flow tiles | Pressure advance".
- Make the test before changing any setting: an unsaved preset edit made here before calibration_generate carries into the test. After it, the test's own edits are its own.

## The three tests

Read the printer, the filament preset and its material from the workspace. Ranges below are mine, and calibration_generate refuses one outside what I accept.

**Temperature.** A tower of blocks, each printed 5 °C cooler than the one below it, labelled with its temperature. start is the bottom block's, the hottest; end the top's; both multiples of 5, start at least 5 hotter. My ranges by material: PLA 230 to 190; ABS and ASA 270 to 230; PETG 250 to 230; PCTG 280 to 240; TPU 240 to 210; PA-CF and PET-CF 320 to 280. Narrow one to the filament's own nozzle_temperature_range_low and nozzle_temperature_range_high when those are tighter (settings_get, filament scope). For another material, centre the range on the preset's nozzle_temperature.
Photograph: the side with the numbers, close enough to read them, in light from one side so strings and droops show. Reading: too hot strings, sags under the overhangs and bridges and looks glossy and blobby; too cold looks rough and dull, bridges poorly, and layers may split. The best block is the coolest one that still bonds and bridges cleanly. It writes nozzle_temperature, and nozzle_temperature_initial_layer kept at the same offset from it the preset had.

**Flow.** Tiles printed at different flow, each with its change embossed on it and in its object name. linear true, the default, is the recommended set, whose tiles add an amount to the flow ratio (-.05 to +.05 on pass 1, finer on pass 2); linear false is the classic set, whose tiles name a percentage change. Start with pass 1; offer pass 2 only when two neighbouring tiles look equally good.
Photograph: the top surfaces from straight above, in light from one side, all tiles in view. Reading: the best tile has a smooth, closed top with no gaps between lines and no ridges or a raised edge. Read filament_flow_ratio with settings_get first: the new value is that plus the tile's amount for the recommended set, or that times (100 + the tile's percentage) / 100 for the classic set. It writes filament_flow_ratio.

**Pressure advance.** method tower, the default, prints a tower whose pressure advance rises by step for each millimetre of height from start at the bottom; line prints numbered lines; pattern prints numbered corners. Leave start, end and step to calibration_generate's defaults unless the person asks; give extruderType bowden for a printer that feeds through a long tube, otherwise leave it. Bambu Lab printers measure this themselves before a print when flow dynamics calibration is on, and the value they measure stays on the printer: say so before offering the test on one.
Photograph: tower: the corners from the side, with a ruler beside it or the height where they look best; line or pattern: from straight above, numbers in view. Reading: the best height or line has sharp corners with no bulge before them and no gap or thin wall after them. For the tower the value is start plus the best height in millimetres times step; for line and pattern, the number by the best one. It writes pressure_advance, with enable_pressure_advance on.

What I made is in the workspace: the plate's calibration carries the test and its range, and the objects are the test pieces. Call setup_record with the project's name as the purpose, the one name the test has everywhere (such as "Calibration · Gray PETG · Prusa MK4"), and the test and its range as the headline (such as "Temperature tower, 240 → 210 °C in 5 °C blocks; read the cleanest block"). Say what you would set in a sentence, with no Choices line, since the card holds the choices. When the person picks another, preview that one instead.

When they have not named it, use the printer's model alone. When it is already that copy, from an earlier test, save into it under its own name: never a second copy. When it is a preset of the person's own, ask whether to write the result into it or save it as a copy with that name, and do what they choose.

The test changed some of the filament's settings for itself. When the preview warns saves_unsaved_edits, it lists them with their saved values: put each one you are not writing into the same patch at its saved value, so the preset keeps only the result.

The app's note says when the person saved it, and under what name. Call setup_record with the same purpose and the test and range followed by the result as the headline, such as "Temperature tower, 230 → 190 °C in 5 °C blocks; result 215 °C saved", so the test's card keeps it. Say the preset's name exactly, since the filament menu may shorten it. Say that this test project uses it now, that other projects keep their filament until the person picks this one for them, and that it can be changed back. Then offer the next test in the order above as a reply choice, without starting it.

When the app's note says the person pressed Undo on the receipt, the save is taken back as the note says. Ask what they would pick instead, and propose again only with their answer."},"state":"succeeded"}

# Issues I report about the print

The rules above still apply. This request is the first to carry something I reported about the print: the person pressed Ask AI on a print-issue chip (their message has a <print_issue> block), or a slice finished with warnings that plate's last slice did not have (the plate's sliceWarnings, in the workspace and in a tool result's slicing section, counts what the chip shows; slice_report's findings section has the full list, and also the timelapse warnings, marked appliesWhen "timelapse", which the chip does not count).

The chip's button sends "Explain this issue and my options.": a question, so answer it and leave the project as it is. When the person then asks you to fix it, change what the issue names, and only that; anything else worth changing is a suggestion.

How to read a finding. A blocker means I will not slice or print until it is fixed; a warning means the slice exists and can print; a critical warning is one I flag as serious. The setting key names what to change, and settings_search or settings_get with that key tells what the setting is and its value now. The object, when named, narrows where; with none it is about the plate or the setup. count says how many warnings there are; read slice_report's findings when more than the first matters. An ignored one is a finding the person chose not to be told about again: still true of the slice. Explain a finding from its words, never from a cause you supply.

A warning is my statement about the slice, not proof the print will fail. Say what it risks for this print and its purpose. Some are the person's call because they trade the look, the time or their hardware: adding support (marks on the surface, clean-up), re-orienting, a filament pairing, a nozzle. A setting that only shapes the toolpath is yours to settle when the request covers it.

A finding counts as resolved only when a new slice no longer reports it, never because a setting changed or a chip was closed or ignored. Asked whether the print is ready, name what the slice still warns about.

| What I report while slicing | What it usually means, and where it points |
| --- | --- |
| "It seems object … has floating regions / floating cantilever / large overhangs. Please re-orient the object or enable support generation."; "Your model needs support!" | Parts start in the air or overhang far and will sag or fail without support. Support settings (enable_support, support_type) or orientation; which one is the person's call. |
| "Object can't be printed for empty layer between … and …" (critical) | Layers with nothing printed: features thinner than a line, or a broken mesh. object_analyze, object_repair, layer height or line widths. |
| "… is too close to others, and collisions may be caused."; "Prime Tower is too close to others"; "too close to exclusion area" | The nozzle or head may hit an object, the tower or a no-go area. Position (object_place, plate_layout) or print_sequence. |
| "Found gcode path conflicts between object … and …" (critical) | Two objects' paths cross. Spacing or layout. |
| "A G-code path goes beyond plate boundaries." / "… beyond the max print height." | A skirt, brim, support or the object itself leaves the printable area by a little (more is a blocker). Position, brim_width, skirt_distance or size. |
| Speed, acceleration, jerk or junction deviation above the printer's maximum ("JusPrin will automatically cap …"); "Setting the jerk speed too low …" | It prints with the motion capped to the printer's limits. The setting named, or the printer's machine_max_* values. |
| A support base pattern replaced ("Rectilinear will be used instead") | I substitute a pattern this support type cannot use. support_base_pattern. |
| "Partial flushing volume set to 0 …"; "PLA and PETG filaments detected in the mixture …"; filament shrinkage or XY size compensation "will not be used"; different nozzle and filament diameters with the prime tower | Multi-filament settings: colours may mix, or a setting is dropped for this plate. Flushing volumes, the filaments chosen, the setting named. |
| "The nozzle hardness required by the filament is higher than …" | An abrasive filament wears the installed nozzle. Physical, the person's call: nozzle or filament. |
| Traditional timelapse "may cause surface imperfections"; smooth timelapse with the prime tower off | Only for a print that records a timelapse, which is chosen when it is sent; the chip does not count these. timelapse_type, enable_prime_tower. |

When the person describes a problem in a print they made that points at the filament or its settings (stringing, gaps, bulging corners), the calibration skill says whether a test is worth it.

I raise no slicing warning for thin walls, bridges, bed adhesion, brims or cooling. When the person asks about those, read slice_report's firstLayer, islands and supports sections and the settings; never present one as a warning I gave.

**Flow.** Tiles printed at different flow, each with its change embossed on it and in its object name. linear true, the default, is the recommended set, whose tiles add an amount to the flow ratio (-.05 to +.05 on pass 1, finer on pass 2); linear false is the classic set, whose tiles name a percentage change. Start with pass 1; offer pass 2 only when two neighbouring tiles look equally good.
Photograph: the top surfaces from straight above, in light from one side, all tiles in view. Reading: the best tile has a smooth, closed top with no gaps between lines and no ridges or a raised edge. Read filament_flow_ratio with settings_get first: the new value is that plus the tile's amount for the recommended set, or that times (100 + the tile's percentage) / 100 for the classic set. It writes filament_flow_ratio.

**Pressure advance.** method tower, the default, prints a tower whose pressure advance rises by step for each millimetre of height from start at the bottom; line prints numbered lines; pattern prints numbered corners. Leave start, end and step to calibration_generate's defaults unless the person asks; give extruderType bowden for a printer that feeds through a long tube, otherwise leave it. Bambu Lab printers measure this themselves before a print when flow dynamics calibration is on, and the value they measure stays on the printer: say so before offering the test on one.
Photograph: tower: the corners from the side, with a ruler beside it or the height where they look best; line or pattern: from straight above, numbers in view. Reading: the best height or line has sharp corners with no bulge before them and no gap or thin wall after them. For the tower the value is start plus the best height in millimetres times step; for line and pattern, the number by the best one. It writes pressure_advance, with enable_pressure_advance on.

All three write the filament preset.

## After making a test

What I made is in the workspace: the plate's calibration carries the test and its range, and the objects are the test pieces. Call setup_record with the project's name as the purpose, the one name the test has everywhere (such as "Calibration · Gray PETG · Prusa MK4"), and the test and its range as the headline (such as "Temperature tower, 240 → 210 °C in 5 °C blocks; read the cleanest block"). Then tell the person to slice and print it as usual, what to photograph and how, and to send the photo here.

When the app's note says the person reopened this test project, its steps are gone, as the note says. Say when it was generated, that reopening does not bring back its per-block temperatures (or pressure-advance steps), so slicing it now would print the whole tower at one setting, and offer to make it again with the same range. End with "Choices: Regenerate tower | Just look at it". On "Regenerate tower", call calibration_generate with the same test and range: that reply is the go-ahead, since the person agreed to the test when it was first made. On "Just look at it", leave the project as it is. Otherwise, while the plate carries calibration, its steps are in place. A flow test keeps its tiles' ratios and the pressure-advance pattern its G-code; neither needs anything.

## Reading the photo and saving the result

Name the best block, tile or height and why, and the runner-up. If the photo cannot show it (blurry, too far, the wrong side), ask for another before guessing. Then propose one write: settings_preview_patch on the filament preset in use, with persistAs. The app shows the person that preview as a card with Save preset and Pick another, and saves exactly what it previewed when they press Save preset: never call settings_apply_patch for it. Say what you would set in a sentence, with no Choices line, since the card holds the choices. When the person picks another, preview that one instead.

The name: when the preset in use comes with the app, save a copy named "<filament preset> · <printer> calibrated", with the printer named as the person names it (such as "Bambu PLA Basic · Prusa MK4 calibrated"): their own printer's name, or the words they used for it, never a printer preset's name with its nozzle ("Bambu Lab X1 Carbon 0.4 nozzle"). When they have not named it, use the printer's model alone. When it is already that copy, from an earlier test, save into it under its own name: never a second copy. When it is a preset of the person's own, ask whether to write the result into it or save it as a copy with that name, and do what they choose.

The test changed some of the filament's settings for itself. When the preview warns saves_unsaved_edits, it lists them with their saved values: put each one you are not writing into the same patch at its saved value, so the preset keeps only the result.

## After saving

The app's note says when the person saved it, and under what name. Call setup_record with the same purpose and the test and range followed by the result as the headline, such as "Temperature tower, 230 → 190 °C in 5 °C blocks; result 215 °C saved", so the test's card keeps it. Say the preset's name exactly, since the filament menu may shorten it. Say that this test project uses it now, that other projects keep their filament until the person picks this one for them, and that it can be changed back. Then offer the next test in the order above as a reply choice, without starting it.

When the app's note says the person pressed Undo on the receipt, the save is taken back as the note says. Ask what they would pick instead, and propose again only with their answer."},"state":"succeeded"}

settingItems.description:
How the density changes from the surface to the center of the object.
Linear: the density changes at a constant rate.
Quadratic: the density stays close to the sparse infill density near the surface and changes faster towards the center.
Exponential: the d
settingItems.label: Adaptive gradient

settingItems.description: Density of the adaptive infill at the center of the object.
settingItems.label: Interior density

settingItems.description:
Grades the Gyroid and TPMS infill inside the object: its cells grow from the surface of the object towards its center. The sparse infill density is used at the surface and the interior density at the center.
Distance warp, Smooth blend and Stepped shells f
settingItems.label: Adaptive density (experimental)

settingItems.description:
Aligns infill, bridge, ironing, and top/bottom surface directions to follow the model's orientation on the build plate.
When enabled, these directions rotate together with the model so the printed features keep their intended orientation relative to the pa
settingItems.label: Align directions to model

settingItems.description:
This factor affects the amount of material for bottom solid infill.

The actual bottom solid infill flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.
settingItems.label: Bottom surface flow ratio

settingItems.description: This option will auto-detect narrow internal solid infill areas. If enabled, the concentric pattern will be used for the area to speed up printing. Otherwise, the rectilinear pattern will be used by default.
settingItems.label: Detect narrow internal solid infills

settingItems.description: Insert solid infill at specific layers. Use N to insert every Nth layer, N#K to insert K consecutive solid layers every N layers (K is optional, e.g. '5#' equals '5#1'), or a comma-separated list (e.g. 1,7,9) to insert at explicit layers. Layers are 1-base
settingItems.label: Insert solid layers

settingItems.description: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' infills. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. If the walls are printed with transparent filament, the mixed color infill will be visible. It will not take effect unless t
settingItems.label: Flush into objects' infill

settingItems.description: This is the speed for gap infill. Gaps usually have irregular line width and should be printed more slowly.
settingItems.label: Gap infill

settingItems.description: This disables supporting bridges, which decreases the amount of support required. Bridges can usually be printed directly without support over a reasonable distance.
settingItems.label: Don't support bridges

settingItems.description: This enables support generation.
settingItems.label: Enable support

settingItems.description: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' support. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. It will not take effect unless a prime tower is enabled.
settingItems.label: Flush into objects' support

settingItems.description: Support layer uses layer height independent with object layer. This is to support customizing Z-gap and save print time. This option will be invalid when the prime tower is enabled.
settingItems.label: Independent support layer height

settingItems.description: Same as "Small perimeters", but for supports. This separate setting will affect the speed of support for areas <= `small_support_perimeter_threshold`. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 80%), it will be calculated on the support or support interfac
settingItems.label: Small support perimeters

settingItems.description: This sets the threshold for small support perimeter length. The default threshold is 0mm.
settingItems.label: Small support perimeters threshold

settingItems.description: Use this setting to rotate the support pattern on the horizontal plane.
settingItems.label: Pattern angle

settingItems.description:
Line pattern of support.

The Default option for Tree supports is Hollow, which means no base pattern. For other support types, the Default option is the Rectilinear pattern.

NOTE: For Organic supports, the two walls are supported only with the Hollow/Def
settingItems.label: Base pattern

settingItems.description: This determines the spacing between support lines.
settingItems.label: Base pattern spacing

settingItems.description:
Density of internal solid infill for Elephant foot layers compensation.
The initial value for the second layer is set.
Subsequent layers become linearly denser by the height specified in elefant_foot_compensation_layers.
settingItems.label: Elephant foot layers density

settingItems.description:
Maximum layer height for the combined sparse infill.

Set it to 0 or 100% to use the nozzle diameter (for maximum reduction in print time) or a value of ~80% to maximize sparse infill strength.

The number of layers over which infill is combined is derived
settingItems.label: Infill combination - Max layer height

settingItems.description: Height of the first layer. Making the first layer height thicker can improve build plate adhesion.
settingItems.label: First layer height

settingItems.description: The height of the beams of the interlocking structure, measured in number of layers. Less layers is stronger, but more prone to defects.
settingItems.label: Interlocking beam layers

settingItems.description: This is the height for each layer. Smaller layer heights give greater accuracy but longer printing time.
settingItems.label: Layer height

settingItems.description: Enable this to get precise Z height of object after slicing. It will get the precise object height by fine-tuning the layer heights of the last few layers. Note that this is an experimental parameter.
settingItems.label: Precise Z height

settingItems.description:
Start height of the scarf.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current layer height. The default value for this parameter is 0.
settingItems.label: Scarf start height

settingItems.description: Number of skirt layers: usually only one
settingItems.label: Skirt height

settingItems.description: If enabled, consecutive layers on which the prime tower has no filament change are printed as a single thicker tower layer instead of one thin layer each, the same way infill combination merges sparse infill. The merged layer is printed at the top of the r
settingItems.label: Combine sparse layers

settingItems.description: The number of layers on which the elephant foot compensation will be active. The first layer will be shrunk by the elephant foot compensation value, then the next layers will be linearly shrunk less, up to the layer indicated by this value.
settingItems.label: Elephant foot compensation layers

settingItems.description:
This option enables the generation of an extra bridge layer over internal and/or external bridges.

Extra bridge layers help improve bridge appearance and reliability, as the solid infill is better supported. This is especially useful in fast printers, whe
settingItems.label: Extra bridge layers (beta)

settingItems.description:
This factor affects the amount of material on the first layer for the extrusion path roles listed in this section.

For the first layer, the actual flow ratio for each path role (does not affect brims and skirts) will be multiplied by this value.
settingItems.label: First layer flow ratio

settingItems.description: Whether to apply fuzzy skin on the first layer.
settingItems.label: Apply fuzzy skin to first layer

settingItems.description: This is the printing acceleration for the first layer. Using limited acceleration can improve build plate adhesion.
settingItems.label: First layer

settingItems.description: This is the speed for the first layer except for walls and brim, such as infill, gap fill and support.
settingItems.label: First layer infill

settingItems.description: Jerk for the first layer.
settingItems.label: First layer

settingItems.description: Line width of the first layer. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.
settingItems.label: First layer

settingItems.description: The minimum wall width that should be used for the first layer is recommended to be set to the same size as the nozzle. This adjustment is expected to enhance adhesion.
settingItems.label: First layer minimum wall width

settingItems.description:
Density of the bottom surface layer. Intended for aesthetic or functional purposes, not to fix issues such as over-extrusion.
WARNING: Lowering this value may negatively affect bed adhesion.
settingItems.label: Bottom surface density

settingItems.description:
Direction in which bottom surfaces are filled when using a center-based pattern (Concentric, Spiral Inset, Archimedean Chords, Octagram Spiral).
Inward starts each surface with the wider outer curves, which improves first layer adhesion on build plates whe
settingItems.label: Bottom surface fill order

settingItems.description: Combine multiple brims into one when they are close to each other. This can improve brim adhesion.
settingItems.label: Combine brims

settingItems.description: Generate interlocking beam structure at the locations where different filaments touch. This improves the adhesion between filaments, especially models printed in different materials.
settingItems.label: Use beam interlocking

settingItems.description: The distance from the boundary between filaments to generate interlocking structure, measured in cells. Too few cells will result in poor adhesion.
settingItems.label: Interlocking depth

settingItems.description: This expands the first raft or support layer to improve bed adhesion.
settingItems.label: First layer expansion

settingItems.description:
Applies the cyclic toolchange order to the first layer as well.
By default this is disabled, because the first layer is instead ordered for the best bed adhesion: filaments that print small, fragile first-layer features are printed last, so the following t
settingItems.label: Apply cyclic order to first layer

settingItems.description:
The geometry will be decimated before detecting sharp angles. This parameter indicates the minimum length of the deviation for the decimation.
0 to deactivate.
settingItems.label: Brim ear detection radius

settingItems.description:
Maximum angle to let a brim ear appear.
If set to 0, no brim will be created.
If set to ~180, brim will be created on everything but straight sections.
settingItems.label: Brim ear max angle

settingItems.description: Generate mouse ears only on the outer contour of the model, excluding holes and enclosed sections.
settingItems.label: Brim ears outer only

settingItems.description:
This factor affects the amount of material for brims.

The actual brim flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

Note: The resulting value will not be affected by the first-layer flo
settingItems.label: Brim flow ratio

settingItems.description: This creates a gap between the innermost brim line and the object and can make the brim easier to remove.
settingItems.label: Brim-object gap

settingItems.description: This controls the generation of the brim at outer and/or inner side of models. Auto means the brim width is analyzed and calculated automatically.
settingItems.label: Brim type

settingItems.description:
When enabled, the brim is aligned with the first-layer perimeter geometry after Elephant Foot Compensation is applied.
This option is intended for cases where Elephant Foot Compensation significantly alters the first-layer footprint.

If your current setup
settingItems.label: Brim follows compensated outline

settingItems.description: This is the distance from the model to the outermost brim line.
settingItems.label: Brim width

settingItems.description:
Belt printers only. Widens the brim SIDEWAYS, across the belt, without extending it further ahead of or behind the object. Use it when a part needs more grip along its length than Brim width alone gives.

Measured on the belt surface, and added on top of B
settingItems.label: Extra brim width

settingItems.description: Temperature difference to be applied when an extruder is not active. The value is not used when 'idle_temperature' in filament settings is set to non-zero value.
settingItems.label: Temperature variation

settingItems.description: When interface-layer temperature boost is active, set the nozzle back to print temperature at the start of the prime tower so it cools down during the tower.
settingItems.label: Cool down from interface boost during prime tower

settingItems.description: This option will drop the temperature of the inactive extruders to prevent oozing.
settingItems.label: Enable

settingItems.description:
Speed of the externally visible bridge extrusions.

In addition, if Slow down for curled perimeters is disabled, it will be the print speed of overhang walls that are supported by less than 13%, whether they are part of a bridge or an overhang.
settingItems.label: External

settingItems.description: Enable this option to slow down when printing overhangs. The speeds for different overhang percentages are set below.
settingItems.label: Slow down for overhangs

settingItems.description: This is the speed for the walls and brim of the first layer.
settingItems.label: First layer

settingItems.description: Travel speed of the first layer.
settingItems.label: First layer travel speed

settingItems.description: This is the speed for inner walls.
settingItems.label: Inner wall

settingItems.description: Speed of internal bridges. If the value is expressed as a percentage, it will be calculated based on the bridge_speed. Default value is 150%.
settingItems.label: Internal

settingItems.description: This is the speed for internal solid infill, not including the top or bottom surface.
settingItems.label: Internal solid infill

settingItems.description: This is the print speed for ironing lines.
settingItems.label: Ironing speed

settingItems.description:
This setting adds an extra wall to every other layer. This way the infill gets wedged vertically between the walls, resulting in stronger prints.

When this option is enabled, the ensure vertical shell thickness option needs to be disabled.

Using lightnin
settingItems.label: Alternate extra wall

settingItems.description: This detects the overhang percentage relative to line width and uses a different speed to print. For 100% overhang, bridging speed is used.
settingItems.label: Detect overhang walls

settingItems.description: This detects thin walls which can’t contain two lines and uses a single line to print. It may not print as well because it’s not a closed loop.
settingItems.label: Detect thin walls

settingItems.description: This allows the infill area to be enlarged slightly to overlap with walls for better bonding. The percentage value is relative to the inner wall line width. Set this value to ~10-15% to minimize potential over extrusion and accumulation of material resulti
settingItems.label: Infill/wall overlap

settingItems.description: Acceleration of inner walls.
settingItems.label: Inner wall

settingItems.description:
Filament to print inner walls.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.
settingItems.label: Inner walls

settingItems.description:
This factor affects the amount of material for inner walls.

The actual inner wall flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.
settingItems.label: Inner wall flow ratio

settingItems.description: Jerk of inner walls.
settingItems.label: Inner wall

settingItems.description: Line width of inner wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.
settingItems.label: Inner wall

settingItems.description:
This value governs the thickness of the external (visible) bridge layer.
Values above 1.0: Increase the amount of material while maintaining line spacing. This can improve line contact and strength.
Values below 1.0: Reduce the amount of material while adj
settingItems.label: Bridge flow ratio

settingItems.description:
Enables gap fill for the selected solid surfaces. The minimum gap length that will be filled can be controlled from the filter out tiny gaps option below.

Options:
1. Everywhere: Applies gap fill to top, bottom and internal solid surfaces for maximum stre
settingItems.label: Apply gap fill

settingItems.description:
Controls the density (spacing) of internal bridge lines.

- Higher than 100% density (Recommended Max 125%):
  - Pros: Impr
settingItems.label: Internal bridge density

settingItems.description:
This value governs the thickness of the internal bridge layer. This is the first layer over sparse infill so increasing it may increase strength and upper layer quality.
Values above 1.0: Increase the amount of material while maintaining line spacing. This
settingItems.label: Internal bridge flow ratio

settingItems.description: Use scarf joint to minimize seam visibility and increase seam strength.
settingItems.label: Scarf joint seam (beta)

settingItems.description:
If enabled, bridge extrusion uses a line height equal to the nozzle diameter.
This increases bridge strength and reliability, allowing longer spans, but may worsen appearance.
If disabled, bridges may look better but are generally reliable only for shorter
settingItems.label: Thick external bridges

settingItems.description:
If enabled, internal bridge extrusion uses a line height equal to the nozzle diameter.
This increases internal bridge strength and reliability when printed over sparse infill, but may worsen appearance.
If disabled, internal bridges may look better but can
settingItems.label: Thick internal bridges

settingItems.description:
In order to reduce the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, the loop is interrupted and shortened by a specified amount.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the nozzle diameter. The default value for this paramet
settingItems.label: Seam gap

settingItems.description: This is the starting position for each part of the outer wall.
settingItems.label: Seam position

settingItems.description: Apply scarf joints only to smooth perimeters where traditional seams do not conceal the seams at sharp corners effectively.
settingItems.label: Conditional scarf joint

settingItems.description: The scarf extends to the entire length of the wall.
settingItems.label: Scarf around entire wall

settingItems.description: Use scarf joint for inner walls as well.
settingItems.label: Scarf joint for inner walls

settingItems.description: Length of the scarf. Setting this parameter to zero effectively disables the scarf.
settingItems.label: Scarf length

settingItems.description: Minimum number of segments of each scarf.
settingItems.label: Scarf steps

settingItems.description: This option causes the inner seams to be shifted backwards based on their depth, forming a zigzag pattern.
settingItems.label: Staggered inner seams

settingItems.description:
Controls the density (spacing) of external bridge lines.
Theoretically, 100% means a solid bridge, but due to the tendency of bridge extrusions to sag, 100% may not be sufficient.

- Higher than 100% density (Recommended Max 125%):
  - Pros: Produces smoot
settingItems.label: External bridge density

settingItems.description:
Enable this option to slow down printing in areas where perimeters may have curled upwards.
For example, additional slowdown will be applied when printing overhangs on sharp corners like the front of the Benchy hull, reducing curling which compounds over m
settingItems.label: Slow down for curled perimeters

settingItems.description: This is the line pattern of bottom surface infill, not including bridge infill.
settingItems.label: Bottom surface pattern

settingItems.description: Choose this option if you want to completely fill in the tops of the infill pattern
settingItems.label: Fill pattern tops

settingItems.description: This is the angle for sparse infill pattern, which controls the start or main direction of lines.
settingItems.label: Sparse infill direction

settingItems.description: Line pattern of internal solid infill. if the detect narrow internal solid infill be enabled, the concentric pattern will be used for the small area.
settingItems.label: Internal solid infill pattern

settingItems.description: Angle for solid infill pattern, which controls the start or main direction of line.
settingItems.label: Solid infill direction

settingItems.description: This parameter adds a rotation of solid infill direction to each layer according to the specified template. The template is a comma-separated list of angles in degrees, e.g. '0,90'. The first angle is applied to the first layer, the second angle to the sec
settingItems.label: Solid infill rotation template

settingItems.description: Density of internal sparse infill, 100% turns all sparse infill into solid infill and internal solid infill pattern will be used.
settingItems.label: Sparse infill density

settingItems.description: This is the line pattern for internal sparse infill.
settingItems.label: Sparse infill pattern

settingItems.description: Belt printers only. Extends the brim AHEAD of the object along the belt, on every downhill-facing edge of its contact area - both the object's first contact with the belt and any island that lands later. This apron is laid onto the belt before the object r
settingItems.label: Leading brim length

settingItems.description:
A draft shield is useful to protect an ABS or ASA print from warping and detaching from print bed due to wind draft. It is usually needed only with open frame printers, i.e. without an enclosure.

Enabled = skirt is as tall as the highest printed object. O
settingItems.label: Draft shield

settingItems.description: If enabled, all printing extruders will be primed at the front edge of the print bed at the start of the print.
settingItems.label: Prime all printing extruders

settingItems.description:
Print sequence of the internal (inner) and external (outer) walls.

Use Inner/Outer for best overhangs. This is because the overhanging walls can adhere to a neighbouring perimeter while printing. However, this option results in slightly reduced surface qu
settingItems.label: Walls printing order

settingItems.description: The number of layers, including the bottom surface layer, that take the color painted on a bottom surface. Set to 0 to use the bottom shell layers. A value larger than the bottom shell also colors the sparse infill above the painted area.
settingItems.label: Bottom paint penetration layers

settingItems.description:
Fixed angle for the bottom solid infill lines.
Set to -1 to follow the default solid infill direction.
settingItems.label: Bottom layer direction

settingItems.description: This is the number of solid layers of bottom shell, including the bottom surface layer. When the thickness calculated by this value is thinner than bottom shell thickness, the bottom shell layers will be increased.
settingItems.label: Bottom shell layers

settingItems.description: Enable mixed color sublayer splitting. When enabled, layers containing mixed color filaments will be split into sub-layers to achieve color mixing effects.
settingItems.label: Mixed color sublayer

settingItems.description: Tightens the gyroid wave along the Z (vertical) axis at low infill density to shorten the effective vertical column length and improve Z-axis compression buckling resistance. Filament use is preserved. No effect at ~30% sparse infill density and above. Onl
settingItems.label: Z-buckling bias optimization (experimental)

settingItems.description:
Noise type to use for fuzzy skin generation:
Classic: Classic uniform random noise.
Perlin: Perlin noise, which gives a more consistent texture.
Billow: Similar to perlin noise, but clumpier.
Ridged Multifractal: Ridged noise with sharp, jagged features. C
settingItems.label: Fuzzy skin noise type

settingItems.description:
Travel acceleration of first layer.
The percentage value is relative to Travel Acceleration.
settingItems.label: First layer travel

settingItems.description:
Travel jerk of first layer.
The percentage value is relative to Travel Jerk.
settingItems.label: First layer travel

settingItems.description: Using multiple lines for the infill pattern, if supported by infill pattern.
settingItems.label: Fill Multiline

settingItems.description: The remaining part of the model contour after removing a certain depth from the surface is called the skeleton. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section. When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skeleton densi
settingItems.label: Skeleton infill density

settingItems.description: The portion of the model's outer surface within a certain depth range is called the skin. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section. When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skin densities, this area will not b
settingItems.label: Skin infill density

settingItems.description:
Line width of the Bridge. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.
Recommended to use with a higher Bridge density or Bridge flow ratio.

The maximum value is 100% or the nozzle diameter.
If set to 0, the line width will match the
settingItems.label: Bridge

settingItems.description:
This option can help reduce pillowing on top surfaces in heavily slanted or curved models.
By default, small internal bridges are filtered out and the internal solid infill is printed directly over the sparse infill. This works well in most cases, speeding
settingItems.label: Filter out small internal bridges

settingItems.description: Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. JusPrin tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter se
settingItems.label: Sparse infill anchor length

settingItems.description: Automatically combine sparse infill of several layers to print together in order to reduce time. Walls are still printed with original layer height.
settingItems.label: Infill combination

settingItems.description: Sparse infill areas which are smaller than this threshold value are replaced by internal solid infill.
settingItems.label: Minimum sparse infill threshold

settingItems.description: Acceleration of sparse infill. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 100%), it will be calculated based on the default acceleration.
settingItems.label: Sparse infill

settingItems.description: This is the density of the first raft or support layer.
settingItems.label: First layer density

settingItems.description: Density of top surface layer. A value of 100% creates a fully solid, smooth top layer. Reducing this value results in a textured top surface, according to the chosen top surface pattern. A value of 0% will result in only the walls on the top layer being cr
settingItems.label: Top surface density

settingItems.description:
Chooses where the centering point of centered top/bottom surface patterns (Archimedean Chords, Octagram Spiral) is placed.
 - Each Surface: centers the pattern on every individual surface region, so each island is symmetric on its own.
 - Each Model: cente
settingItems.label: Center surface pattern on

settingItems.description: The pattern that will be used when ironing.
settingItems.label: Ironing Pattern

settingItems.description: This covers the top contact layer of the supports with loops. It is disabled by default.
settingItems.label: Loop pattern interface

settingItems.description: This is the line pattern for support interfaces. The default pattern for non-soluble support interfaces is Rectilinear while the default pattern for soluble support interfaces is Concentric.
settingItems.label: Interface pattern

settingItems.description: The pattern that will be used when ironing.
settingItems.label: Support Ironing Pattern

settingItems.description: The first few layers are printed slower than normal. The speed is gradually increased in a linear fashion over the specified number of layers.
settingItems.label: Number of slow layers

settingItems.description:
Extrude perimeters that have a part over an overhang in the reverse direction on even layers. This alternating pattern can drastically improve steep overhangs.

This setting can also help reduce part warping due to the reduction of stresses in the part wal
settingItems.label: Overhang reversal

settingItems.description:
Apply the reverse perimeters logic only on internal perimeters.

This setting greatly reduces part stresses as they are now distributed in alternating directions. This should reduce part warping while also maintaining external wall quality. This feature ca
settingItems.label: Reverse only internal perimeters

settingItems.description: Object will be raised by this number of support layers. Use this function to avoid warping when printing ABS.
settingItems.label: Raft layers

settingItems.description: Create additional perimeter paths over steep overhangs and areas where bridges cannot be anchored.
settingItems.label: Extra perimeters on overhangs

settingItems.description: The angle of the infill angled lines. 60° will result in a pure honeycomb.
settingItems.label: Infill overhang angle

settingItems.description: Maximum overhang angle for Lightning infill support propagation.
settingItems.label: Lightning overhang angle

settingItems.description: Modify the geometry to print overhangs without support material.

settingItems.label: Make overhangs printable - Maximum angle
